title: Upper bound for the optimality parameter
statement: For each natural number $q$, set $\alpha=1/(q+2)$ and let $t$ be the standard Gaussian upper-tail quantile with upper-tail mass $\alpha$. Choose a dimension $N=r+1$ for which the upper-tail indicator of the normalized sum of $N$ independent uniform signs has mass within $\alpha/2$ of $\alpha$ and level-one Fourier weight within half the square of the Gaussian density at $t$ of that square. If $\Delta$ is twice the mass of this upper-tail indicator in dimension $N$, then $\Delta<3\alpha$.
